key_insight: LLMberjack provides an interactive, human-guided way to trim reply trees from debates into coherent linear multi-party dialogues while preserving speaker identity and discourse relations, with optional LLM assistance for message and speaker edits.
problem_solved: Converts complex reply-tree debates into usable, coherent linear conversations for dataset creation and evaluation, addressing loss of participant identity and discourse structure when linearizing multi-branch discussions.
method: Interactive visualization of discussion reply trees allowing users to select and trim branches into a linear dialogue sequence.
Linearization algorithm that preserves participant identity and discourse relations while reordering and pruning messages.
Optional LLM-assisted editing to rewrite messages and generate/clarify speaker descriptions in-context during trimming.
impact: Enables scalable, high-quality creation of multi-party conversational data and controlled dialogues for training and evaluating conversational models, combining human judgment with LLM automation to improve realism and labeling efficiency.
visual_elements: Before/after diagram: reply tree on the left and resulting linearized conversation on the right
UI mockup showing interactive tree visualization, color-coded participants, and trimming controls
Flowchart of the human-in-the-loop + optional LLM editing pipeline
Concrete example card: original debate snippet and the edited final multi-party dialogue
paper_title: LLMberjack: Guided Trimming of Debate Trees for Multi-Party Conversation Creation
paper_authors: Leonardo Bottona, Nicolò Penzo, Bruno Lepri, Marco Guerini, Sara Tonelli
